sections.name: Hook
lines: db_hook
In 1971, a man hijacked a plane, collected two hundred thousand dollars, and jumped out into the night. He was never seen again.
db_title
This is the mystery of D.B. Cooper.

sections.name: The flight
lines: db_seat
November 24th, 1971. The night before Thanksgiving. A quiet man in a dark suit boards a flight from Portland to Seattle, under the name Dan Cooper.
db_note
He hands a flight attendant a note. She thinks he's flirting, and slips it into her pocket. He leans in. Miss, you'd better look at that note.
db_case
I have a bomb, he says, and opens his briefcase. Inside, wires, and red sticks. He wants two hundred thousand dollars, and four parachutes.

sections.name: The swap
lines: db_seattle
In Seattle, the FBI delivers the cash and the parachutes. Cooper lets all thirty six passengers go.
db_takeoff
Then he orders the plane back into the sky, heading south, flying low and slow.

sections.name: The jump
lines: db_stairs
Somewhere over the forests of southwest Washington, in the dark and the rain, he lowers the rear stairs.
db_jump
And he jumps. When the plane lands, the cabin is empty. Cooper, and the money, are gone.

sections.name: The clue
lines: db_boy
Nine years later, an eight year old boy named Brian Ingram is helping his family build a campfire on a Columbia River beach.
db_money
He digs into the sand, and finds bundles of rotting twenty dollar bills. About fifty eight hundred dollars. The serial numbers match Cooper's ransom.

sections.name: Still unsolved
lines: db_files
It was the first real clue in years. But it raised more questions than it answered. In 2016, the FBI stopped actively investigating.
db_outro
Did he survive the jump? Nobody knows. What do you think happened to D.B. Cooper? Follow for more true crime, animated.
